# `sim/ai/AIHitDetection.js`

> **Source:** `engine/sim/ai/AIHitDetection.js`

AIHitDetection.js - Advanced Hit Detection for Spells and Projectiles Features: - Swept sphere/capsule collision (prevents tunneling) - Time of impact calculation for accurate VFX - Damage falloff curves (linear, quadratic, inverse square) - Multiple hitbox types (sphere, capsule, AABB) - Spatial hashing for efficient broad phase Based on industry best practices: - Conservative Advancement (Bullet Physics) - GJK-based swept tests - Motion clamping for CCD

## Classes

### `class SpatialHash`

Spatial hash for efficient broad-phase collision detection

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor(cellSize = DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE)` |  |
| `hash` | `hash(x, y, z)` | Hash a world position to cell key |
| `clear` | `clear()` | Clear all entries |
| `insert` | `insert(entity, position)` | Insert an entity at a position |
| `remove` | `remove(entityId)` | Remove an entity |
| `queryRadius` | `queryRadius(position, radius)` | Query all entities within radius of a position |
| `queryPath` | `queryPath(start, end, radius)` | Query entities along a ray/path (for swept collision) |

## Functions

### `sweptSphereSphere(sphereStart, sphereEnd, sphereRadius, targetCenter, targetRadius)`

Swept sphere vs static sphere intersection Finds time t in [0,1] when moving sphere first touches static sphere

**Parameters:**

- `sphereStart` *(number[])* — Moving sphere center at t=0
- `sphereEnd` *(number[])* — Moving sphere center at t=1
- `sphereRadius` *(number)* — Moving sphere radius
- `targetCenter` *(number[])* — Static sphere center
- `targetRadius` *(number)* — Static sphere radius

**Returns:** {t, point, normal} or null if no hit

### `sweptSphereSphereMoving(sphereA, sphereB)`

Swept sphere vs moving sphere intersection Handles both objects moving (relative velocity approach)

**Parameters:**

- `sphereA` *(Object)* — {start, end, radius}
- `sphereB` *(Object)* — {start, end, radius}

**Returns:** {t, point, normal} or null

### `capsuleSphereIntersect(capsuleStart, capsuleEnd, capsuleRadius, targetCenter, targetRadius)`

Swept capsule collision (projectile path as line segment) Creates a capsule from start to end position with given radius

**Parameters:**

- `capsuleStart` *(number[])* — Capsule line start
- `capsuleEnd` *(number[])* — Capsule line end
- `capsuleRadius` *(number)* — Capsule radius
- `targetCenter` *(number[])* — Target sphere center
- `targetRadius` *(number)* — Target sphere radius

**Returns:** {t, point, normal, distance} or null

## Notes & Examples

### Physics Engine Integration

The physics system provides rigid body dynamics, collision detection, and raycasting. Bodies have shapes (box, sphere, mesh), mass properties, and constraints. The GPU physics engine accelerates broad-phase collision detection and particle systems.

**Example: Creating physics bodies**
```js
import { PhysicsWorld } from 'engine/physics/PhysicsWorld.js';
import { RigidBody } from 'engine/physics/RigidBody.js';
import { BoxShape, SphereShape } from 'engine/physics/Shapes.js';

const world = new PhysicsWorld({ gravity: [0, -9.8, 0] });

// Static ground
const ground = new RigidBody({
  type: 'static',
  shape: new BoxShape(10, 1, 10),
  position: [0, -0.5, 0]
});
world.addBody(ground);

// Dynamic box
const box = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  mass: 1,
  shape: new BoxShape(1, 1, 1),
  position: [0, 5, 0],
  restitution: 0.5  // Bounciness
});
world.addBody(box);
```

**Advanced: Collision detection and raycasting**
```js
// Raycast to find what the player is looking at
const hit = world.raycast(camera.position, camera.forward, 100);
if (hit) {
  console.log('Hit entity:', hit.body.entityId);
  console.log('Hit point:', hit.point);
  console.log('Hit normal:', hit.normal);
  
  // Apply impulse at hit point
  hit.body.applyImpulse([0, 10, 0], hit.point);
}

// Shapecast (swept sphere) for character movement
const sweep = world.shapecast(
  player.position,           // Start
  desiredPosition,           // End
  new SphereShape(0.5),    // Player capsule radius
  { ignore: player.body }  // Don't collide with self
);
if (sweep.hit) {
  // Slide along wall
  player.position = sweep.position;
}
```

**Advanced: Constraints and joints**
```js
import { HingeConstraint, FixedConstraint } from 'engine/physics/Constraints.js';

// Door hinge
const doorHinge = new HingeConstraint({
  bodyA: doorFrame,
  bodyB: door,
  pivot: [0, 1, 0],      // Hinge location
  axis: [0, 1, 0],       // Hinge axis (Y up)
  limits: [-90, 90]      // Open angle range in degrees
});
world.addConstraint(doorHinge);

// Ragdoll joint (ball-and-socket)
const shoulder = new FixedConstraint({
  bodyA: torso,
  bodyB: arm,
  pivotA: [0.5, 1.5, 0],  // Shoulder position on torso
  pivotB: [0, 0, 0]       // Shoulder position on arm
});
world.addConstraint(shoulder);
```

**Advanced: Continuous collision detection (CCD)**
```js
// Fast-moving objects need CCD to not tunnel through walls
const projectile = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  shape: new SphereShape(0.1),
  mass: 0.1,
  ccd: { enabled: true, sweptSphereRadius: 0.1 },
  linearDamping: 0  // No air resistance for bullets
});
projectile.velocity = [0, 0, 100];  // Very fast
world.addBody(projectile);
```

**Gotchas:**
- **Units**: Physics uses meters, kilograms, seconds. A 1-unit cube is 1 meter.
- **Time step**: Fixed time step (1/60) gives stable simulation; variable dt causes explosions.
- **Collision layers**: Use collision masks to filter what collides (player vs enemy, bullet vs world).
- **Sleeping**: At-rest bodies sleep to save CPU — wake them before applying forces.
